must_have_5.title: Personal data known
must_have_5.text: Do you know which guest or staff personal data the tool would use?

use_cases.name: Demand forecasting for rooms (by day, guest type and room type)

questions.text: Has the revenue manager agreed to review the forecasts every week?
questions.why: Forecasts drift with events and market changes; without a weekly review, errors go unnoticed.

questions.text: Can the revenue team spot a forecast that looks wrong and correct it?
questions.why: The tool cannot know about a local event or a lost group; a person must correct it.

questions.text: Do you know the monthly fee, often charged per room, and any set-up fee?
questions.why: Revenue tools are usually priced per room, so the cost grows with hotel size.

questions.text: Does the tool receive new bookings and cancellations automatically from your booking system (PMS)?
questions.why: A forecast built on bookings typed in by hand is always out of date.

questions.text: Do you have at least one year of booking and cancellation history in your booking system?
questions.why: A demand forecast learns from last year's pattern; with less history it guesses.

questions.text: Is it written who may change a forecast by hand?
questions.why: Unrecorded manual changes make it impossible to learn whether the tool or the person was wrong.

questions.text: Are big local events and group bookings for the next year entered in your systems?
questions.why: Events drive demand spikes the history cannot show.

use_cases.name: Dynamic room pricing, including automatic rate publishing

questions.text: Has the owner or general manager set the lowest and highest price the tool may publish?
questions.why: Automatic pricing without limits can publish a rate far too low or too high in minutes.

questions.text: Can the revenue manager tell when to switch automatic pricing off, for example during a crisis?
questions.why: In unusual weeks the tool's logic breaks; a person must judge when to take over.

questions.text: Do you know the pricing-tool fee and any extra channel-manager fees?
questions.why: Publishing rates to booking sites often adds a second fee.

questions.text: Can the pricing tool send new rates to your booking system and channel manager straight away?
questions.why: Automatic pricing only works if new rates reach every sales channel at once.

questions.text: Are your rate plans and booking restrictions set up the same way in every system?
questions.why: Messy rate plans make the tool push the wrong price to the wrong room.

questions.text: Does the pricing tool receive competitor rates automatically every day?
questions.why: Pricing without competitor rates ignores the market.

questions.text: In a managed or franchised hotel, has the owner agreed in writing to automatic pricing?
questions.why: Owners often hold the right to approve pricing strategy.

questions.text: Can one named person switch automatic rate publishing off at once?
questions.why: A pricing error spreads to every booking site within minutes.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Has the revenue manager agreed to own the pricing tool day to day?
questions.why: Automatic prices need one person watching them daily.

use_cases.name: Competitor rate tracking and market insight with machine learning

questions.text: Has the revenue or sales manager agreed to read competitor rates at least weekly?
questions.why: Rate data no one reads has no value.

questions.text: Has the team agreed which competitor hotels to compare with?
questions.why: Comparing with the wrong hotels leads to wrong price decisions.

questions.text: Do you know the monthly fee for the rate-tracking tool?
questions.why: Rate-tracking tools are priced by number of competitors and checks per day.

questions.text: Can competitor rates go straight into your pricing tool or a report?
questions.why: Copying rates by hand takes hours and is soon out of date.

questions.text: Is each competitor room type matched to the closest of your room types?
questions.why: A suite compared with a standard room gives a false price gap.

questions.text: Has the vendor explained how it collects competitor prices and how often?
questions.why: Prices collected rarely or from one site can mislead.

use_cases.name: AI assistants for revenue questions, reports and price explanations

questions.text: Has the revenue team been shown how to ask the assistant questions?
questions.why: Vague questions get vague or wrong answers.

questions.text: Do staff check the assistant's numbers against your reports before acting on them?
questions.why: AI assistants can state a wrong figure confidently.

questions.text: Have you checked whether your revenue tool or reporting licence already includes this?
questions.why: Many revenue tools now include an assistant at no extra cost.

questions.text: Can the assistant read your revenue and booking data directly?
questions.why: Without your data it can only give general advice.

questions.text: Are key figures, such as occupancy and revenue per room, defined the same way everywhere?
questions.why: If definitions differ, the assistant mixes numbers that do not match.

questions.text: Can the assistant show which report or number each answer comes from?
questions.why: Staff can only check an answer if they can see its source.

questions.text: Is it agreed who corrects the assistant when it gives a wrong figure?
questions.why: Wrong figures repeated in meetings lead to wrong price decisions.

use_cases.name: AI agents that watch revenue, recommend and act

questions.text: Has a senior revenue person agreed to check the agents' work every day?
questions.why: Agents act on rates; daily checks catch mistakes before they cost money.

questions.text: Can the senior revenue person set what the agents may do and review what they did?
questions.why: Limits only help if someone can set and check them.

questions.text: Do you know the usage fees and the cost of connecting the agents to your systems?
questions.why: Usage-based fees can rise fast when agents run all day.

questions.text: Can the agents read and change data in your booking system and channel manager?
questions.why: An agent that cannot act in your systems cannot do the job.

questions.text: Do rates and availability match across your booking system and channel manager today?
questions.why: Agents copy errors faster than people do.

questions.text: Is it written which rate changes need a person's approval first?
questions.why: Large rate changes should never happen without a person.

questions.text: Is every action the agents take recorded so you can check it later?
questions.why: Without a record you cannot find or undo a bad change.

questions.text: Can the senior revenue person stop the agents immediately if they misbehave?
questions.why: Agents keep acting until someone stops them.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

use_cases.name: Total revenue and budget forecasting, including function space

questions.text: Have the finance and revenue leads agreed to own the forecast together?
questions.why: Total-revenue forecasts cross departments; one side alone will miss half.

questions.text: Can the finance team build budgets from forecasts and compare different scenarios?
questions.why: The value is in testing "what if" cases, not one number.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the reporting and forecasting tool?
questions.why: Forecasting is often sold as part of a reporting licence.

questions.text: Can the tool read data from rooms, meeting rooms, restaurants and bars?
questions.why: Total revenue needs every outlet, not only rooms.

questions.text: Do you have at least one year of revenue history for every outlet and meeting room?
questions.why: Outlets without history cannot be forecast.

questions.text: Do all departments use one agreed definition of revenue?
questions.why: If F&B and rooms count revenue differently, totals are wrong.

use_cases.name: Price optimisation for upsells and extras

questions.text: Has the revenue or front-office manager agreed to own the upsell offers?
questions.why: Offers need someone to adjust them as demand changes.

questions.text: Can the team read which offers guests accept and adjust them?
questions.why: Offers no one accepts waste guest attention.

questions.text: Do you know whether the tool charges commission per sale or a subscription?
questions.why: Commission eats into each upsell; subscription costs even with no sales.

questions.text: Can the tool see which rooms and extras are free in your booking system?
questions.why: Selling an upgrade that is not available creates angry guests.

questions.text: Are prices for room upgrades and extras up to date in one place?
questions.why: The tool can only price what it can see.

questions.text: Is it written which offers the tool may price by itself?
questions.why: Without a rule the tool may discount your best rooms.

questions.text: Do front-desk staff know which offers guests accepted before arrival?
questions.why: Staff must honour what guests bought in advance.

use_cases.name: Spa and wellness yield management and demand-based treatment prices

questions.text: Have the spa manager and revenue manager agreed to own treatment pricing together?
questions.why: Spa knows the therapists; revenue knows pricing.

questions.text: Does the spa team understand how prices that change with demand work?
questions.why: Staff must explain to guests why prices differ by time.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the spa-system add-on?
questions.why: Usually an add-on to the spa booking system.

questions.text: Is your spa booking system linked to your hotel booking system?
questions.why: Hotel occupancy drives spa demand.

questions.text: Are treatment bookings, therapist schedules and no-shows recorded in the spa system?
questions.why: Demand pricing needs past treatment demand.

questions.text: Are the rules for treatment prices, including lowest prices, written down?
questions.why: Unlimited price swings damage trust in the spa.

questions.text: Have therapists been told how changing prices may affect their schedules?
questions.why: Busy peak hours change therapist workloads.

use_cases.name: Rate parity checks (same price on all channels) and automatic matching

questions.text: Has the revenue or online sales manager agreed to own price-check alerts?
questions.why: Alerts no one reads change nothing.

questions.text: Does the revenue manager know the price terms agreed with each booking site?
questions.why: Whether a lower price breaks a deal depends on each contract.

questions.text: Do you know the monthly fee for the price-check tool?
questions.why: Usually priced per hotel.

questions.text: Can the tool read your rates from the booking engine and channel manager?
questions.why: It must compare your own rates with what sites show.

questions.text: Are your own rates by channel, room type and conditions recorded in one place?
questions.why: The tool needs your true price to spot differences.

questions.text: Is there a written lowest price the tool may never go below when matching?
questions.why: Automatic matching can chase prices down.

questions.text: Is one person named to contact a booking site that shows a lower price?
questions.why: Someone must fix the cause, not only the symptom.

questions.text: Can one named person turn off automatic price matching at once?
questions.why: Matching a wrong price can undercut your own rates on every site.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

use_cases.name: AI voice agents for reservation and front-desk calls (hotel and central lines)

questions.text: Has the reservations manager agreed to listen to a sample of calls every week?
questions.why: Call quality drops unnoticed unless someone listens.

questions.text: Can your team update the agent's answers the same day prices or policies change?
questions.why: A voice agent quoting last month's price loses bookings.

questions.text: Do you know the set-up fee and the price per call or per minute?
questions.why: Per-minute pricing makes busy months expensive.

questions.text: Can the agent connect to your phone system and transfer calls to staff?
questions.why: Without transfer, guests get stuck with the agent.

questions.text: Can the agent read live availability and create bookings in your booking system?
questions.why: An agent that cannot book only takes messages.

questions.text: Are your answers to common guest questions written down and current?
questions.why: The agent can only answer what it has been given.

questions.text: Is it written what the voice agent may do alone, such as booking or cancelling?
questions.why: Cancellations and refunds need a clear limit.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Can one named person send all calls back to staff with one switch?
questions.why: If the agent misbehaves, guests must reach people straight away.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Has a person checked the rates, policies and directions the voice agent tells callers?
questions.why: Callers book on what the agent says.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Can callers reach a staff member at any time by asking for one?
questions.why: Upset or complex callers must reach a person.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

use_cases.name: AI handling of reservation emails and offers

questions.text: Have the reservations agents agreed to review the drafts the tool writes?
questions.why: Drafts save time only if agents trust and use them.

questions.text: Can agents spot a wrong price, date or room type in a draft?
questions.why: The most costly mistakes in offers are price and dates.

questions.text: Do you know the price per user or per email?
questions.why: Email volume pricing grows with season.

questions.text: Is the tool connected to your reservations mailbox?
questions.why: It must read guest emails to draft replies.

questions.text: Can the tool read live rates and availability from your booking system?
questions.why: Offers with old rates must be honoured or cause disputes.

questions.text: Are rate rules, room descriptions and offer templates written down and current?
questions.why: The tool copies whatever it is given.

questions.text: Does a person check every price before an offer is sent?
questions.why: A sent price is a promise to the guest.

use_cases.name: AI channel management (sending rates and availability to booking channels)

questions.text: Is one person named to decide which rooms and rates go to each booking site?
questions.why: The tool sends what you decide; it does not set strategy.

questions.text: Do you know the monthly fee for the channel manager?
questions.why: Often priced by number of booking sites connected.

questions.text: Does the channel manager exchange bookings and availability both ways with your booking system?
questions.why: A one-way link causes double bookings.

questions.text: Is every room and rate matched to the right code on each booking site?
questions.why: A wrong match sells the wrong room at the wrong price.

questions.text: Does someone check daily that prices on booking sites match what you set?
questions.why: Errors on one site can run for days unnoticed.

questions.text: Has the vendor shown which changes the tool makes by itself, such as closing sales on a site?
questions.why: Many channel managers have little or no AI; know what you pay for.

questions.text: Is one person named to act on channel-manager alerts every day?
questions.why: Channel errors sell rooms at the wrong price within hours.

questions.text: Can the revenue team spot a booking site showing a wrong price or closed rooms?
questions.why: Channel errors are cheap if caught the same day.

use_cases.name: AI assistant and personalisation in the website booking engine

questions.text: Has the online sales or marketing manager agreed to own the booking-engine assistant?
questions.why: Someone must keep its answers and offers current.

questions.text: Can the online sales manager see how many visitors book and where others leave?
questions.why: Shows whether the assistant helps or hurts bookings.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the booking-engine add-on?
questions.why: Usually a monthly add-on or a fee per booking.

questions.text: Is the booking engine linked to your booking system for live availability?
questions.why: Offering rooms that are sold out loses trust.

questions.text: Are room descriptions, photos, extras and prices on the booking engine complete and current?
questions.why: The assistant answers from this content.

questions.text: Has a person checked what the booking assistant tells visitors about rooms and extras?
questions.why: Visitors book on its answers.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Can website visitors reach the reservations team from the booking assistant?
questions.why: Some guests only book after talking to a person.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Is it written which offers and extras the booking assistant may suggest?
questions.why: Stops the assistant pushing offers you do not want to sell.

use_cases.name: Predicting cancellations and no-shows to set overbooking

questions.text: Has the revenue manager agreed to set the overbooking limit each day?
questions.why: Too much overbooking means guests sent elsewhere.

questions.text: Can the team weigh the cost of moving a guest against the extra revenue?
questions.why: Moving a loyal guest can cost more than the room earns.

questions.text: Have you checked whether your revenue tool already includes this?
questions.why: Usually part of the revenue management tool.

questions.text: Is the forecasting tool linked to your booking system?
questions.why: It needs live bookings to predict cancellations.

questions.text: Do you have cancellation and no-show history by booking site and room type?
questions.why: No-show rates differ a lot between booking sites.

questions.text: Is there an agreed plan with front office for moving a guest to another hotel?
questions.why: When overbooking goes wrong, the desk must act at once.

use_cases.name: AI for group rooming lists, rate loading and reservation tasks

questions.text: Has the group reservations coordinator agreed to check the tool's work?
questions.why: Group errors affect dozens of rooms at once.

questions.text: Does the group coordinator know your group contracts and rate codes well?
questions.why: Only someone who knows the contract can spot a wrong rate.

questions.text: Do you know whether this is a booking-system add-on or a separate tool, and its cost?
questions.why: Add-ons are usually cheaper to run.

questions.text: Can the tool create group blocks and load rates in your booking system?
questions.why: The value is in not typing rooming lists by hand.

questions.text: Are your rate codes and rooming-list formats tidy and the same every time?
questions.why: Messy formats make the tool guess.

questions.text: Does a person check every bulk change before it is saved?
questions.why: One wrong bulk change can break a whole group.

use_cases.name: Bookable hotel apps inside AI assistants (such as ChatGPT apps)

questions.text: Has the online sales or distribution lead agreed to own this new sales channel?
questions.why: New channels fail without someone watching results.

questions.text: Does the distribution lead understand how guests book through AI assistants such as ChatGPT?
questions.why: The team must know how guests will find and book you.

questions.text: Do you know the build or vendor fee and any commission per booking?
questions.why: Commission may be similar to booking sites.

questions.text: Can AI assistants read your live rates and availability through a booking link?
questions.why: Without live data the assistant shows wrong prices.

questions.text: Are your hotel description, photos and rates complete and current online?
questions.why: Assistants describe you from this content.

questions.text: Do you know which company runs the booking link inside the AI assistant?
questions.why: Someone must fix it when bookings fail.

questions.text: Is it written which rates and rooms AI assistants may sell?
questions.why: Stops the channel from selling rooms you want to keep.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Can you take the hotel off AI assistants quickly if bookings go wrong?
questions.why: Wrong bookings keep coming in until the link is closed.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

use_cases.name: AI scoring and analysis of reservation calls

questions.text: Is it agreed that call scores are used only for coaching, not pay or discipline?
questions.why: Staff accept coaching tools; they resist hidden performance ratings.

questions.text: Can the reservations manager turn call results into useful coaching sessions?
questions.why: Scores without coaching change nothing.

questions.text: Do you know the price per call analysed?
questions.why: Busy lines make per-call pricing add up.

questions.text: Is the tool linked to your phone and call-recording systems?
questions.why: It analyses recordings; no recordings, no analysis.

questions.text: Are your call standards written down, so the tool scores against them?
questions.why: Without your standards, the tool scores against its own idea of a good call.

questions.text: Are calls already recorded and stored in one place?
questions.why: The tool needs recordings to work.

questions.text: Have reservations staff been told about the tool and asked for feedback before it starts?
questions.why: Staff who learn about call scoring late lose trust in management.

questions.text: Can a staff member see and question their own call scores?
questions.why: People accept scores they can see and challenge.

use_cases.name: AI-written marketing text and translation

questions.text: Has one person agreed to check that AI texts match your brand's tone?
questions.why: AI text drifts towards bland, generic wording.

questions.text: Can the marketing team edit AI drafts so they sound like your hotel?
questions.why: Editing, not prompting, is what makes the text usable.

questions.text: Have you checked whether you already pay for an AI writing tool?
questions.why: Many office licences already include one.

questions.text: Can staff put approved texts and translations on your website without help from an agency?
questions.why: If only an agency can publish, AI texts sit unused.

questions.text: Are your brand guidelines and approved hotel facts written down in one place?
questions.why: The tool invents details when facts are missing.

questions.text: Does a person check facts such as prices, opening times and green claims before publishing?
questions.why: AI writes wrong facts confidently; guests hold you to them.

questions.text: Does a native speaker check translations for your main guest languages?
questions.why: Machine translation errors look careless to guests.

use_cases.name: Handling group and event enquiries and requests for proposals

questions.text: Has the sales manager agreed to review every proposal before it is sent?
questions.why: Proposals carry prices and dates the hotel must honour.

questions.text: Can the sales team check the room, menu and price details in AI drafts?
questions.why: The costly mistakes are wrong prices and dates.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the proposal add-on for your sales and events system?
questions.why: Usually an add-on priced per user.

questions.text: Can the tool read your meeting-room calendar in your sales and events system?
questions.why: Offering a room already booked creates a double booking.

questions.text: Does the tool receive enquiries from your inbox and event-booking platforms?
questions.why: Enquiries outside the tool get missed.

questions.text: Are meeting-room details, menus and pricing rules recorded and current?
questions.why: The draft can only be as good as these facts.

questions.text: Does the tool hold meeting rooms only after a person confirms the booking?
questions.why: A proposal must not promise rooms that are already taken.

use_cases.name: Guest grouping, predictive targeting, loyalty and personalised email campaigns

questions.text: Has the marketing or loyalty manager agreed to own guest campaigns?
questions.why: Campaigns need someone to judge results.

questions.text: Can the team read campaign results and adjust guest groups?
questions.why: Groups that do not respond should change.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the guest-database tool?
questions.why: Guest databases are usually priced per guest profile.

questions.text: Is your guest database filled automatically from your booking system and restaurant tills?
questions.why: Typed-in data is always incomplete.

questions.text: Are guest records merged so each guest appears only once?
questions.why: Duplicates mean the same guest gets three emails.

questions.text: Does a person approve every campaign before it is sent?
questions.why: A wrong guest group or offer reaches thousands at once.

questions.text: Do you know your email open and booking rates today, to compare against?
questions.why: Without a starting figure you cannot show the tool helped.

use_cases.name: AI-made images and video for marketing

questions.text: Has a brand owner agreed to approve every AI image before use?
questions.why: One wrong image can spread fast online.

questions.text: Can the team spot an AI image that makes the hotel look better than it is?
questions.why: Guests who arrive to something different write bad reviews.

questions.text: Do you know the licence cost of the image tool?
questions.why: Usually a monthly licence per user.

questions.text: Do you have recent, good-quality photos of your hotel to feed into the tool?
questions.why: AI images built from real photos stay true to the hotel.

questions.text: Is it written that no image may show something guests will not find?
questions.why: The main risk is a misleading picture.

questions.text: Can the image tool deliver the sizes your website and social channels need?
questions.why: Otherwise staff redo every image by hand.

use_cases.name: Optimising paid ads, metasearch and automated ad buying

questions.text: Has the digital marketing manager or your agency agreed to own ad spending?
questions.why: Automated ad buying needs someone watching spend weekly.

questions.text: Can the digital marketing manager see how much booking revenue each ad brings in?
questions.why: Without this, the tool spends on ads that do not sell rooms.

questions.text: Is there a monthly ad-spend limit the tool cannot go above?
questions.why: Automated bidding can spend a month's budget in days.

questions.text: Does your booking engine report which ads led to bookings?
questions.why: The tool learns only from bookings it can see.

questions.text: Do you have at least three months of booking results from your ads?
questions.why: Too little data makes the tool bid at random.

questions.text: Is there a written agreement with the agency on fees and who controls the ad accounts?
questions.why: Hotels lose their ad history when an agency leaves.

use_cases.name: Visibility in search engines and AI assistants (SEO, GEO)

questions.text: Has the marketing or online sales lead agreed to own online visibility?
questions.why: Visibility work never ends; someone must own it.

questions.text: Does the online sales lead know what makes a hotel appear in AI search answers?
questions.why: The rules differ from classic search.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the monitoring tool and the content work?
questions.why: Content work is usually the larger cost.

questions.text: Does your website describe rooms, prices and location in a way search tools can read?
questions.why: AI search tools quote what they can read easily.

questions.text: Are your hotel facts the same on your website and every listing?
questions.why: AI tools mix sources; one wrong listing spreads.

questions.text: Does someone check each month how AI assistants describe your hotel?
questions.why: You cannot fix what you never check.

use_cases.name: Finding, qualifying and scoring sales leads (groups, events, companies)

questions.text: Has the sales team agreed to work the leads the tool ranks highest?
questions.why: Scores only help if sales act on them.

questions.text: Can sales staff question a lead score that looks wrong?
questions.why: The tool cannot know relationships your team has.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of lead scoring in your sales system?
questions.why: Often a higher plan of the sales system.

questions.text: Do you have a sales system that records leads and deals?
questions.why: The tool scores leads from this system.

questions.text: Do you have records of past leads, both won and lost?
questions.why: It learns what a good lead looks like from your past.

questions.text: Has the vendor shown how current and accurate its company contact data is?
questions.why: Out-of-date contacts waste the sales team's time.

use_cases.name: Digital check-in with ID document scan (online, mobile or kiosk)

questions.text: Can desk staff check in any guest whose scan or online check-in fails?
questions.why: Guests stuck at a failed kiosk is the worst first impression.

questions.text: Can desk staff recognise an ID scan that looks wrong?
questions.why: A false or misread ID must be caught by a person.

questions.text: Do you know the fee per check-in and any kiosk hardware cost?
questions.why: Kiosks add a hardware cost to the per-use fee.

questions.text: Does the tool send guest details straight into your booking system?
questions.why: Typing scanned details again removes the time saving.

questions.text: Does the tool fill in the guest registration form you use today?
questions.why: Staff should not type the same guest details twice.

questions.text: Are guest names and booking details correct before arrival, so scans match them?
questions.why: Wrong booking names make every scan fail at the desk.

questions.text: Is it agreed what desk staff do when an ID scan does not match the booking?
questions.why: Guests should not wait while staff improvise.

use_cases.name: AI room assignment

questions.text: Can desk staff judge when to keep or change the tool's room choice?
questions.why: Staff know guests the tool does not.

questions.text: Have you checked whether your booking system or upsell tool already includes this?
questions.why: Often already included.

questions.text: Can the tool see free rooms and housekeeping status as they change?
questions.why: Assigning a dirty room delays check-in.

questions.text: Are guest room preferences and past stays recorded in your booking system?
questions.why: Good assignment depends on knowing preferences.

questions.text: Is it written that staff may change the room the tool chooses?
questions.why: Staff must not feel bound by the tool.

questions.text: Is it agreed who checks the tool's room choices, and how often?
questions.why: Spot checks find patterns such as always giving one floor.

questions.text: Has the front-office manager agreed to own the room-assignment rules?
questions.why: Someone must keep the rules in line with sales and upgrade policy.

use_cases.name: Biometric face check at check-in (selfie matched to ID photo)

questions.text: Can guests who say no to the face check be checked in another way?
questions.why: Some guests will refuse; they must not be stuck.

questions.text: Can desk staff handle a failed face match calmly and quickly?
questions.why: A failed match feels like an accusation to the guest.

questions.text: Do you know the fee per check and any kiosk hardware cost?
questions.why: Per-check fees add up in busy hotels.

questions.text: Is the identity-check service linked to your check-in process?
questions.why: A separate step adds time instead of saving it.

questions.text: Has the vendor shown the face check works equally well for guests of every age and skin tone?
questions.why: A check that fails for some guests embarrasses them at the desk.

questions.text: Is one person named to handle guests who complain about the face check?
questions.why: Complaints about face checks escalate fast if nobody owns them.

use_cases.name: AI assistants and agents for the front desk and property management system

questions.text: Have front-office staff been shown how to use the assistant in daily work?
questions.why: Unused assistants are the most common failure.

questions.text: Has a supervisor agreed to check what the assistant changes in the booking system?
questions.why: Changes in bookings affect guests directly.

questions.text: Can staff check and undo a change the assistant made in the booking system?
questions.why: Mistakes must be easy to reverse.

questions.text: Do you know the add-on or usage fee?
questions.why: Often charged per user or per action.

questions.text: Can the assistant make changes in your booking system, with its own login?

questions.why: Groups change covers more than anything else.

questions.why: Matching is only as good as these records.

questions.text: Can staff see why they were matched to a hotel and ask for a change?
questions.why: Staff accept matches they understand.

questions.text: Is housing or travel for seasonal staff arranged with each match?
questions.why: Seasonal staff need a place to live.

use_cases.name: Face or fingerprint time clocks for staff attendance

questions.text: Has the HR manager agreed to own the time clocks?
questions.why: Clocks affect pay.

questions.text: Can staff choose a card or PIN instead of face or fingerprint?
questions.why: Many staff object to biometrics.

questions.text: Can IT remove a leaver from the time clocks on their last day?
questions.why: Leavers who can still clock in create wrong hours.

questions.text: Do the clocks send hours to payroll and scheduling?
questions.why: Retyped hours cause pay errors.

questions.text: Are attendance records kept in one place and checked against rotas?
questions.why: Attendance must match planned shifts.

questions.text: Is the money approved to buy or lease, install and maintain the clocks?
questions.why: Terminals are a one-off cost.

questions.text: Have staff been told about the clocks and asked for feedback before they start?
questions.why: Biometric clocks worry staff.

questions.text: Is it agreed what staff do when the clock does not recognise them?
questions.why: Staff must still be able to clock in.

use_cases.name: Business performance dashboards (KPIs) with AI analysis

questions.text: Have the GM and department heads agreed to use the dashboard in weekly meetings?
questions.why: Dashboards help only when used to decide.

questions.text: Is one person named to decide how each key figure is calculated?
questions.why: Different definitions make figures unreliable.

questions.text: Can managers question a figure or AI comment that looks wrong?
questions.why: AI comments can sound right and be wrong.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the reporting software?
questions.why: Usually per user.

questions.text: Does the dashboard receive data from your booking, finance and till systems automatically?
questions.why: Manual uploads make dashboards stale.

questions.text: Is one manager named to act on each dashboard alert?
questions.why: Alerts without owners change nothing.

questions.text: Do your booking, finance and till systems use the same outlet and department names?
questions.why: Mismatched names break the dashboard figures.

use_cases.name: Generative AI assistants for managers and head-office staff

questions.text: Do managers check AI answers before using them in decisions or emails?
questions.why: AI assistants make up facts confidently.

questions.text: Do you know the licence cost per manager for the business AI assistant?
questions.why: Usually per user per month.

questions.text: Is the business version set up in your company's own account?
questions.why: Business versions keep your data out of public tools.

questions.text: Are document access rights set so the assistant shows people only what they may see?
questions.why: The assistant can surface documents to the wrong person.

questions.text: Have you listed the first tasks managers will use the assistant for, such as reports or emails?
questions.why: A short starting list shows value quickly.

questions.text: Can managers share instructions that work well for the assistant with each other?
questions.why: Shared examples spread good use across the team.

questions.text: Has the GM agreed to sponsor the assistant and use it themselves?
questions.why: Managers follow what the GM uses.

questions.text: Is one person named to manage the assistant's licences and settings?
questions.why: Licences sprawl and settings drift without an owner.

use_cases.name: Meeting, briefing and report automation

questions.text: Does someone check every summary or report before it is shared?
questions.why: Summaries can drop or invent points.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the add-on?
questions.why: Often an add-on to reporting.

questions.text: Can the tool read data from your booking system or reports?
questions.why: Briefings need daily figures.

questions.text: Are daily figures, such as arrivals and VIPs, available each morning?
questions.why: Briefings use these figures.

questions.text: Is it agreed which meetings the tool joins and summarises?
questions.why: Staff should know which meetings the tool joins.

questions.text: Have you chosen which recurring meetings or reports to automate first?
questions.why: Starting with one daily briefing shows quickly whether it works.

questions.text: Has one manager agreed to own the automated briefings and reports?
questions.why: Someone must fix a wrong briefing before it spreads.

use_cases.name: Company-wide AI and data platforms in hotel groups

questions.text: Is one group AI lead named, with a central team behind them?
questions.why: Three owners means no owner.

questions.text: Does the central team include people who connect systems and manage data?
questions.why: Platforms fail on data, not AI.

questions.text: Is a multi-year budget for the programme agreed at group level?
questions.why: This is a large programme.

questions.text: Do your hotels' systems already send data to one central place?
questions.why: No central data, no platform.

questions.text: Do all hotels in the group use the same definitions for key figures?
questions.why: Comparing hotels needs the same definitions.

questions.text: Is there a written group plan for which AI uses come first?
questions.why: Without priorities, money spreads thin.

questions.text: Is each new AI use reviewed for risk before it starts?
questions.why: A central check stops repeated mistakes.

use_cases.name: Reporting to owners and asset managers

questions.text: Has the asset manager or finance lead agreed to own owner reports?
questions.why: Owners judge the hotel on these reports.

questions.text: Does the asset manager know the report format each owner expects?
questions.why: Owners compare hotels in their own format.

questions.text: Do you know the subscription cost of the owner-reporting tool?
questions.why: Usually priced per hotel.

questions.text: Does the tool receive data from every operator or management company automatically?
questions.why: Manual collection is the work you want to remove.

questions.text: Do all operators use the same account codes, or is there a mapping between them?
questions.why: Different codes make hotels impossible to compare.

questions.text: Is there a written owner-operator agreement on what data is shared?
questions.why: Operators may refuse data without it.

questions.text: Does a person check every owner report before it is sent?
questions.why: Owners act on these numbers.

use_cases.name: Assistant answering frontline staff questions on handbooks and procedures

questions.text: Have department heads agreed to keep their procedures current in the assistant?
questions.why: Old procedures give staff wrong answers.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the staff-app add-on?
questions.why: Usually per user.

questions.text: Can frontline staff reach the assistant on their phones or a shared device?
questions.why: Frontline staff rarely sit at a desk.

questions.text: Are your handbooks and work instructions written down and current?
questions.why: The assistant answers from these only.

questions.text: Does the assistant show which handbook page each answer comes from?
questions.why: Staff can check answers before acting.

questions.text: Can staff ask the assistant questions in their own language?
questions.why: Many frontline teams speak several languages.

questions.text: Do staff know to ask a supervisor when an answer seems wrong?
questions.why: Wrong procedures repeated by staff cause real mistakes.

questions.text: Is one person named to approve handbook changes before the assistant uses them?
questions.why: The assistant is only as good as the handbook.

use_cases.name: Internal tools built with AI coding assistants

questions.text: Does each tool built this way have one named person who maintains it?
questions.why: Tools without an owner break and stay broken.

questions.text: Does IT review each tool before staff use it?
questions.why: Home-made tools can open security holes.

questions.text: Can the builders read, test and fix what the coding assistant writes?
questions.why: Code no one understands cannot be maintained.

questions.text: Do you know the cost of the coding assistant and the staff time?
questions.why: Staff time is the larger cost.

questions.text: Can the tools connect to your systems through approved links?
questions.why: Unapproved connections are a security risk.

questions.text: Is there a safe place approved by IT to run the tools?
questions.why: Tools on personal laptops get lost.

questions.text: Does each tool use only the data it needs, with no guest or staff data unless IT agrees?
questions.why: Less data means less damage if something leaks.

questions.text: Are there written rules on what staff may build?
questions.why: Stops risky tools being built.

questions.text: Is it agreed who takes over a tool when its builder leaves?
questions.why: Tools must outlive their builder.

use_cases.name: AI threat detection and automatic response (network, email, computers and phones)

questions.text: Has the IT lead or an outside security provider agreed to watch alerts around the clock?
questions.why: Attacks happen at night and weekends.

questions.text: Does the security team know how to respond when an attack is detected?
questions.why: Detection without response does not stop attacks.

questions.text: Do you know the cost per device or per user?
questions.why: Cost grows with devices.

questions.text: Does the tool cover the network, email and staff computers and phones at every site?
questions.why: One unprotected site is enough for an attacker.

questions.text: Do your systems keep activity records the tool can read?
questions.why: The tool spots attacks in these records.

questions.text: Do you have a written plan for what staff do when a serious alert comes in?
questions.why: A clear plan cuts damage from hours to minutes.

questions.text: Is it agreed which hotel systems the tool may never shut down by itself, such as door locks?
questions.why: Cutting off locks or payments hurts guests.

questions.text: Is it written what the tool may block alone, such as accounts or devices?
questions.why: Blocking the wrong account stops staff working.
questions.origin: v3 gate question, asked here as a plain question

questions.text: Can the IT lead stop the tool's automatic blocking at once?
questions.why: A wrong block can cut staff off from booking or payment systems.

use_cases.name: AI help desk for IT problems

questions.text: Has the IT team agreed to own the AI help desk?
questions.why: Answers need an IT owner.

questions.text: Does the IT team know how to turn common problems into help-desk answers?
questions.why: The AI answers from these.

questions.text: Do you know the subscription cost of the AI help desk?
questions.why: Usually priced per user.

questions.text: Do you have a system that logs IT requests?
questions.why: Requests the AI cannot solve must go somewhere.

questions.text: Are common IT fixes written down in one place?
questions.why: The AI gives only the fixes it has.

questions.text: Does a person approve every password reset and access change the AI suggests?
questions.why: A wrong reset can let an attacker in.

questions.text: Can staff reach a person on the IT team when the AI cannot help?
questions.why: Stuck staff stop working.

use_cases.name: Detecting booking fraud: fake reservations, criminals posing as booking sites, online card fraud

questions.text: Has the revenue or IT security lead agreed to own booking-fraud checks?
questions.why: Fraud attempts need fast decisions.

questions.text: Can staff tell a fake booking-site message from a real one?
questions.why: Fake booking-site messages are a common attack on hotels.

questions.text: Do you know the cost, or whether your payment tools already include it?
questions.why: Often included in payment tools.

questions.text: Can the tool see bookings from your booking engine, booking sites and payment systems?
questions.why: Fraud shows across these systems.

questions.text: Do you keep records of past fraud cases?
questions.why: The tool learns from them.

questions.text: Do staff get regular training on fake emails and messages?
questions.why: Most fraud starts with a fake message.

questions.text: Has IT checked the booking-fraud tool meets your payment provider's card-security requirements?
questions.why: The tool sees card details of bookings.

use_cases.name: AI analysis of security camera video

questions.text: Has the security manager agreed to own the camera alerts?
questions.why: Alerts need an owner.

questions.text: Is someone available to check every alert at any hour?
questions.why: Unchecked alerts give false safety.

questions.text: Are your security cameras and video storage able to run the analysis software?
questions.why: Older cameras often cannot.

questions.text: Is it decided what the tool will look for, such as falls, fire or blocked exits?
questions.why: A clear purpose keeps the tool from watching everything.

questions.text: Is the money approved for any new cameras and the software?
questions.why: Camera upgrades can be costly.

questions.text: Does a person decide what to do about each alert, not the tool?
questions.why: Wrong alerts must not lead to action against guests or staff.

questions.text: Is it agreed that the tool is not used to watch how staff work?
questions.why: Keeps the tool on safety, not monitoring staff.

questions.text: Are camera positions and the areas each one covers recorded?
questions.why: Alerts are useless if nobody knows where the camera is.

use_cases.name: AI network management for guest and staff Wi-Fi

questions.text: Has the IT team or network provider agreed to own Wi-Fi management?
questions.why: Wi-Fi is a top guest complaint.

questions.text: Can the IT team read Wi-Fi performance reports?
questions.why: Reports show where guests struggle.

questions.text: Do you know the cost per Wi-Fi access point?
questions.why: Priced per access point.

questions.text: Can your Wi-Fi equipment be managed centrally?
questions.why: Older equipment cannot.

questions.text: Does your Wi-Fi equipment record how well the network performs?
questions.why: The tool learns from these records.

questions.text: Is one person named to act on Wi-Fi alerts during busy times?
questions.why: Slow Wi-Fi during conferences costs bookings.

questions.text: Are guest and staff Wi-Fi kept on separate networks?
questions.why: A guest device must never reach staff systems.

use_cases.name: Collecting and reporting sustainability (ESG) and carbon data

questions.text: Has the sustainability or engineering lead agreed to own the data and reports?
questions.why: Reports need one owner.

questions.text: Does the sustainability lead know which reports your owner, brand or lenders ask for?
questions.why: Reports differ by who asks.

questions.text: Do you know the subscription cost, or whether a free platform is available in your country?
questions.why: Free platforms exist in some countries.

questions.text: Do meter and supplier data reach the tool automatically?
questions.why: Typing in bills takes days each quarter.

questions.text: Do you record energy, water and waste for each hotel every month?
questions.why: Reports need monthly figures.

questions.text: Is it agreed which reports must go out, to whom and by when?
questions.why: Missed deadlines with owners or brands cause problems.

use_cases.name: Tools for handling guests' requests about their personal data
Generative AI for reviewing contracts

questions.text: Does the contracts or purchasing lead check every AI contract review?
questions.why: AI can miss a risky clause.

questions.text: Does the contracts lead know your contract terms well enough to check the AI's review?
questions.why: Checks need someone who knows your standard terms.

questions.text: Do you know the licence cost per user of the contract-review tool?
questions.why: Usually per user.

questions.text: Are your contract templates and standard positions written down?
questions.why: The AI compares contracts against these.

questions.text: Is it written that contracts go only into the company's approved AI tool?
questions.why: Contracts in public AI tools can leak.

questions.text: Have you decided which contract types go to the AI first, such as supplier contracts?
questions.why: Starting with simple, repeated contracts keeps the risk low.

questions.text: Is a business version of the AI tool set up for contract work?
questions.why: Contracts should not go into personal AI accounts.

use_cases.name: Rules and oversight for using AI

questions.text: Has the general manager or group AI lead agreed to own the AI rules?
questions.why: Rules need a senior owner.

questions.text: Have staff been asked for feedback on the draft AI rules?
questions.why: Rules staff helped shape are followed.

questions.text: Can the person who owns the AI rules write short rules staff will read?
questions.why: Long rules are ignored.

questions.text: Is staff time set aside to write and update the rules?
questions.why: Rules go stale as tools change.

questions.text: Do you have a list of every AI tool staff use, including free ones?
questions.why: You cannot set rules for tools you do not know about.

questions.text: Is it agreed who approves the AI rules?
questions.why: Approval gives the rules weight.

questions.text: Is it agreed how every staff member will be told the rules?
questions.why: Rules no one hears about do nothing.

questions.text: Is a date set to review the rules each year?
questions.why: AI tools change fast.
